build: The Force's crack of the 1990 disk, with Ikari+Talent's trainer, its two options left off (archive.org; side A SHA-1 5597c4896f0a6ada501fb13ad94359063a8c1e29, side B 22f881cff073a4797580f95ca6225903a0bfaa99): all seven levels

exclude: The music player's variables: each voice's place in its playlist and phrase, its note, pitch and counters, and the tempo and volume, set by its init routine and changed every tick

comments.text: JMP $8361: the load coordinator jumps here ($1728, jmp $3FF3) once the play load is in, and this goes on to EngineEntry at $8361.

JMP $89CB, an RTS in The Final Battle's play load. This is the vector StartLevelLoad calls ($1405, jsr $3FF6) before it loads a part, but StartLevelLoad runs only once, when the game starts and before Central Park's first load, while the vector still holds the engine's own JMP $0E00 to the machine set-up. A finished level jumps to CoordinateLevelLoad at $16AD directly ($8533), past that call, so nothing calls this vector while this load is in memory.

The tune's restart flag: the interrupt routine restarts the tune (jsr $4000) when it finds this byte nonzero, clearing it first ($1EEE-$1EF8), and the title sequence clears it at $110D before it starts the tune. The six zero bytes after it, up to the music jumps at $4000, are read by no instruction.
JMP $40EC: the tune's start. The title sequence calls it at $1110 before it plays the tune, and the interrupt routine at $1EF8 when MusicRestartRequest asks for a restart.

JMP $4151: one step of the tune. The interrupt routine calls it at $1F0E on every interrupt, except that while $AB is zero it leaves out every sixth; the title sequence calls it at $111D once a frame, timed by the raster.
JMP $4147: stores A in the player's three control bytes, $4078, $4079 and $407A.

JMP $4257: adds one to $4073. While that byte is not zero the tick routine does not play: it writes the byte to the three voices' control registers ($D404, $D40B, $D412) and the player's control bytes, and returns.
101 bytes of text that nothing reads, carried with the tune: "MUSIC COMPOSED BY REYN OUWEHAND WHILE BEING BUGGED BY FALCO, RICHARD & JOHN! PLAYER/SOUNDS BY FALCO".

The body of MusicInit, which the JMP at $4000 reaches with the song number in A, and the start of the player's code. It multiplies A by eight to index the song table at $4B26, copies the song's first two bytes into the tempo reloads $4076 and $4077, and sets the volume $407C to 15. For each of the three voices it copies the playlist pointer into $409E and $40A1, sets the duration countdown $407D to 1, and clears the playlist place $409B, the phrase place $4098, the repeat count $40A4, the instrument base $4089, the transpose $4095 and the pulse-width switch $40E8; $4075 is set to 1. It then clears the filter switch $40EB, the filter mode bits $407B, the tick divider $4074 and the gate $4073, writes zero to the three voices' control registers ($D404, $D40B, $D412) and to $4078-$407A, and returns. Clobbers: A, X, Y and flags.

Implement Level's $4006 music-control veneer by storing A into the module's three control bytes and returning.
Inputs: A is the control value; the matching retained music occupant and its writable state are active.
Outputs: A is stored to $4078-$407A; A, X, Y, and all status flags are preserved on return.
Clobbers: Memory $4078-$407A; A, X, Y, and flags are preserved, and RTS advances SP by two over the caller's return frame.
Hardware: No hardware registers are written directly.
Copy A into the paired global music-control bytes. Inputs: A is the control value. Outputs: both control bytes equal A; A, X, Y, and flags are preserved. Clobbers: memory only.

Implement Level's $4003 music-tick veneer, honoring the module gate and advancing its sequencer and SID image.
Inputs: The module is initialized; $4073 is its gate byte and the resident IRQ enters through the matching $4003 veneer.
Outputs: Advances or gates the current music tick, updates sequencer/envelope state, emits the resulting SID register values, and returns.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, processor flags, zero-page music cursors, module track/envelope state, and SID register state.
Hardware: Writes SID voice and filter/volume registers as directed by the current tick; no CIA or VIC-II access is introduced by the veneer body.

Implement Level's $4009 gate veneer by incrementing the module gate byte and returning.
Inputs: $4073 is the writable gate byte for the matching retained music occupant.
Outputs: $4073 is incremented modulo 256; N and Z describe the new value; A, X, and Y are preserved.
Clobbers: $4073, N, and Z; A, X, Y, C, V, D, and I are preserved, and RTS advances SP by two over the caller's return frame.
Hardware: No hardware registers are written directly.

Steps the instrument's waveform list and pitch list for voice X, once a tick; the tick routine calls it at $447F for an instrument whose byte 7 has bit 7 set. Byte 1 of the instrument ($49F0, with the record offset from $408F in Y) is the number of both lists: it is written into the operand of the LDY at $459E and picks the waveform list's pointer from $49BE and $49C1. The first time it runs for a note ($4083 still zero) both list places, $40AA and $40AD, are cleared. The waveform list's byte at the place goes to $40A7, the voice's waveform and gate byte, and the place moves on; $FE leaves both as they are, and $FF is followed by the place to go to, whose byte is used. It then goes on into the pitch list at $459E. Clobbers: A, Y, flags and $FE/$FF; X is kept.

[offcut 459F] Self-modified immediate operand of `LDY #$00` at `$459E`. The Final Battle music sequencer writes the selected sequence index here at `$456C`; the following indexed table reads install the sequence pointer in `$FE/$FF`.

The operand of the LDY #$00 at $459E, which the instruction at $456C, earlier in the same routine, rewrites: with the offset of the voice's instrument record from $408F (eleven times the instrument's number) it reads the instrument's byte 1 from the table at $49F0, stores it here, and the LDY then loads it, the number of the instrument's pitch sequence.

Loads the selected four-entry pitch-sequence pointer, reads the current per-voice cursor $40AD, handles $FD/$FE control and $FF redirection, updates frequency-high state $40BC, clears $40B9 and advances the cursor. The $45CD branch advances the cursor then restores the note frequency through $45FE. Uses the instrument-selected index embedded in the preceding LDY operand.

One tick of voice X's arpeggio, called at $4477 when the voice's arpeggio number $40B3 is nonzero and bit 4 of the instrument's flags is clear. Y is the arpeggio number: it picks the list's pointer from $4922 and $492D. The place $40B6 moves on one byte; that byte is added to the note $4092 as a signed number of semitones and the voice's frequency is set to that note's ($45FE). $80 leaves the place and the frequency as they are, and $81 is followed by the place to go to, whose byte is used. Clobbers: A, Y, flags, $FE/$FF, the place $40B6 and the frequency $40B9/$40BC; X is kept.

Set the voice's frequency to a note's. Inputs: Y is the note number and X the voice. Outputs: the low and high bytes from $4863,Y and $48C3,Y go to $40B9,X and $40BC,X, the frequency the tick writes to the voice's $D400/$D401. Clobbers: A and flags.

One tick of a slide for voice X (set up by a phrase's $FB-$FE command), called at $4421 once the note's tick count $4083 reaches the slide's start $40BF. Inputs: Y is the slide speed from $40C2; the step is four times it, a 16-bit amount in $FE/$FF. If the target note $40C5 is at or above the note $4092 the step is added to the voice's frequency $40B9/$40BC, otherwise subtracted. Outputs: once the frequency goes past the target note's, it is set to that note's ($45FE), the speed $40C2 and $40D1 are cleared and the target becomes the voice's note $4092. Clobbers: A, Y, flags and $FE/$FF; X is kept.

One tick of voice X's vibrato, called at $4439 once the note's tick count $4083 reaches the setting's byte 0. Inputs: Y is the vibrato setting's offset, half the instrument's byte 9. The first run for a note ($40D1 zero) only works out the depth, the frequency difference between the note $4092 and the note byte 4 above it, halved as many times as byte 5 says, into $40CB/$40CE, clears the list place $40C8 and sets $40D1. Later runs add byte 6 to the depth while the tick count is at least byte 1 and below byte 7, set the frequency back to the note's ($45FE) and step the up-and-down list that bytes 2 and 3 point at: a byte from 1 to $7F adds the depth that many times, 0 adds nothing, $81 is followed by the place to go to, and any other byte with bit 7 set subtracts it 256 minus that many times; the place moves on. Clobbers: A, Y, flags and $FE/$FF; X is kept.

Conditionally initialize one voice's modulation stream. Inputs: X selects the voice, Y selects its modulation definition, and the current per-voice guard controls initialization. Outputs: when the guard is zero, the modulation cursor and count are cleared and the definition's mode bit is installed; otherwise voice state is unchanged. Clobbers: A and flags, plus indexed voice state only on the initialization path; X and Y are preserved.

One step of voice X's pulse-width sweep (X 0 to 2), or of the filter cut-off when X is 3 (the call at $4465). Y is the instrument's setting, an offset into the filter and pulse settings: their bytes 6 and 7 point at the sweep list, whose entries set the voice's 16-bit value ($40D8 high, $40D4 low) outright or start a run of steps, and the settings' steps move the value up or down between two limits. The frequency is not touched. Clobbers: A, Y, flags, $FE/$FF, $4072 and the voice's place and count in the list ($40E0, $40E4).
0, 7, 14: the offset of each voice's registers from $D400, which the player adds to every SID register address it writes for that voice.
1, 2, 4: each voice's bit in the filter routing, which the player adds to the routing byte it writes to $D417 when an instrument switches the filter on.
23 multiples of eleven, 0 to 242: an instrument command in a phrase adds its number to the voice's instrument base and looks up here the offset of that instrument's eleven-byte record.
Low bytes of the SID frequency for each of the 96 notes, lowest first, read with the note number in Y.
High bytes of the frequencies, read with the same note number. Only 95 are stored: the next table starts where the high byte of the top note would be.

Low bytes of arpeggio pointers 0 to 10, chosen by the number in a phrase's $E0-$F7 command. Pointer 11's low byte is the first byte of the high table after it ($492D), which is also pointer 0's high byte: the two tables overlap by a byte. Pointer 0 ($9DFD) is never followed, since the player skips the arpeggio when the number is 0.

Scene 000, a picture 10 cells wide and 12 high, $4DFA-$52AA: the size byte $AC (width in the high nibble), then 960 bitmap bytes, 120 screen bytes and 120 colour bytes, eight, one and one for each cell. This load holds only its first 6 bytes, $4DFA-$4DFF: the rest comes with the play load, which writes over this one from $4E00 on (here $4E00 is DrawTitleCard).

DrawTitleCard: the loader calls this at $1108 once the last byte of The Final Battle's title load is in, before it starts the tune and waits for Space or fire on either port. It relocates the title's scene pointers (once: TitleRelocateScenePointers at $51A2), sets up the bitmap screen ($140B) and clears the play window's bitmap and its colour copy at $0800 ($140E), then goes on into the renderer below with A = 1, so it draws area 1's scene, scene 4: the level's picture with its name beneath, in the play window beside the status panel. The two NOPs stand where Central Park's RenderScene loads the area from $A2 ($8A52), so A keeps the 1 that the PLA brings back.
two NOPs in place of RenderScene's LDA $A2: A is still 1, area 1

TitleRenderSceneForRoomInA, the title load's copy of Central Park's RenderSceneForRoomInA ($8A54 there), the same instructions with the title's own table addresses. It looks area A up in the area slots at $51E8: the low nibble of the second byte becomes the background colour ($D021 and $32), and the first byte is the scene, whose pointer it reads from $5228 (scenes 0 to 127) or $5328 (128 and up, which no title has). A pointer with bit 15 set returns at once; otherwise the pointer plus the scene base $51E5 is the scene to draw, in $02-$03.

TitleRenderSceneRecordTree, the copy of RenderSceneRecordTree ($8A86 there): sets the window to 30 cells across ($E7) and 18 down ($DC), the nesting depth $38 and the origin $1A-$1B to zero, and goes on into the dispatch loop.

TitleSceneRecordDispatchLoop, the copy of SceneRecordDispatchLoop ($8A96 there): reads the next placement of the composite at $02-$03. $FF ends a composite: at depth zero it returns; deeper, it pulls the parent's place and origin back off the stack, lowers the depth and steps past the placement that led in. Anything else is decoded (TitleDecodeSceneRecord).
TitleAdvanceSceneRecordAndContinue, the copy of AdvanceSceneRecordAndContinue ($8AB1 there): steps $02-$03 past the placement (TitleAdvanceSceneRecordPointer) and goes back to the dispatch loop.

TitleAdvanceSceneRecordPointer, a copy of the play code's AdvanceSceneRecordPointer ($8AB7 in Central Park): adds a placement's length to $02-$03: three bytes, one more when bit 6 of the second byte is set, and one for each colour swap that bits 5 and 6 of the third byte count.

TitleDecodeSceneRecord, the copy of DecodeSceneRecord ($8AD8 there): takes the placement's mirror flag (bit 7 of its second byte, into $E8), its column (the low six bits less 14, plus the origin $1A, into $25) and its row (the low five bits of the third byte less 14, plus $1B, into $26), and looks its scene up in the pointers at $5228. A composite (bit 15 clear) is entered: the origin and the place are pushed, the depth $38 goes up, and the dispatch loop goes on inside it with the placement's column and row as the new origin. A picture (bit 15 set) is drawn by TitleDrawScenePicture, its address in $04-$05.

TitleDrawScenePicture, the copy of the picture drawer that starts at $8B49 in Central Park (RenderUiSceneRecord there). The size byte gives the width (high nibble, $1C) and height (low nibble, $1D) in cells, and a picture wholly outside the window is skipped. It reads the placement's colour swaps, finds the picture's screen bytes and colour bytes after its bitmap bytes, works out where its first visible cell lands in the bitmap, screen RAM, colour RAM and the colour copy at $0800 (the engine's row tables at $1414, $142D, $1446 and $145F), then draws it cell by cell, row by row, clipped at the window's edges. Each cell's screen and colour bytes have the swaps applied (a nibble equal to a swap's low nibble takes its high nibble); its eight bitmap bytes are copied as they are, or, mirrored, in the reverse order of columns and through the pair-reversal table at $1200. A cell whose byte in the colour copy has any of its top three bits set is kept unless the new cell's colour byte is $20 or more, and with bit 4 of it set as well the engine's routine at $1411 merges the two.

This snapshot was saved after it ran: the RTS is in place, and the $00 after it is the operand of the LDA #$00 that it replaced.
